interview.q: In one sentence, what is this site?
interview.a: A site that gives you a one-line rule for CLAUDE.md plus a small hook script so Claude Code stops and asks before it reads your secrets, push to main, deletes and so on, with a pretend £50 reading balance ticking down.

interview.q: Was any of it for you? Which part?
interview.a: Yes, the secrets page. The install-by-asking-Claude-Code prompt with 'show me each change and wait for my yes' is how I would want to do it, and the header comment in the hook is honest about what it does not catch.

interview.q: Did you believe it? What made you believe it, or not?
interview.a: Mostly. It says plainly that the line is only an expectation, that the hook cannot stop a script that opens the file, and the sandbox is the real boundary, and it links Claude Code's own docs. What I did not believe yet is that it would not get in my way, because I never saw the matching rules.

interview.q: Where did you have to guess?
interview.a: What the £50 and 50p are (I only found out on the Start here page that it is not money), why the balance drops as I scroll, whether .env.example or a .env in a service folder is matched, and whether Bash in the matcher means every shell command goes through a Python script.

interview.q: What did you still not know at the end?
interview.a: Which filenames the hook matches, what it does to docker compose or my test runner reading .env, how to remove it, and who riskmandate.ai is. I also never worked out what 'ABP' or RM-R0015 means for me.

interview.q: Was the credit and the price of each page right for what you got?
interview.a: 50p for the secrets page is fine as a number but I could not tell what it bought me. The page says 'read to the end' but the hook box cut off before the part I needed, so I paid for the part I did not need. The start page was the one that actually explained the credit, and it came last.

interview.q: Would you install a behaviour policy from here, today? If not, what would have to change?
interview.a: Not into the payments repo today. I might paste the CLAUDE.md line and the plain permissions deny rule, which are Claude Code's own settings. For the hook I need the full file and a plain list of what it matches (including .env.example and nested .env), plus one line on how to turn it off.
Show the whole hook, uncut, with a short plain-words list: 'blocks these filenames, leaves these alone, to turn it off delete this block'.

interview.q: Would you send this to somebody else? Who?
interview.a: My lead, with a note that the secrets idea is right but the hook needs to be readable first. Not to the juniors yet.

interview.q: Rate the experience from 1 to 5, and say why in one sentence.
interview.a: 3: it answered my question about secrets and told me the truth about its limits, but I could not see what the hook would stop in my daily work and the credit numbers moving as I scrolled were unexplained.

findings.title: The hook source is cut off before the rules that say which files it blocks
findings.detail: The opened 'Read the hook' box ends at the LINE variable with a hard edge, about 25 of the 67 lines. The patterns that decide what is refused (.env.example? nested .env?) are not visible. For someone who will not install what he cannot predict, this is the exact blocker.

findings.title: The matcher includes Bash, Edit and Write with no plain-words reason
findings.detail: The settings.json block shows matcher 'Read|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Grep|Glob|Bash'. A daily user reads that as 'this script sits in front of everything I do', and nothing beside it says it only refuses on credential filenames and stays silent otherwise (that sentence is only in the code comment further down).

findings.title: No word on how to turn the hook off or undo the install
findings.detail: The page after the deny-rule section goes straight to 'Tell us what happened' by email. Nothing says how to remove the hook in seconds if it blocks a deploy, which is the first thing a cautious developer asks before installing.

findings.title: The £50 and the falling balance are unexplained until the third page I open
findings.detail: The home hero says 'you start with £50.00' and '50p of your credit' and the balance in the top bar ticks down as I scroll (£50.00 to £49.99 to £49.87), with no message. 'Nothing is blocked, ever' and no card appear only on Start here. Until then it reads as possible real money.

findings.title: The typing terminal demo shows nothing useful and looks stuck
findings.detail: On the home page and on the policy page the terminal box sits at 'Install the b' or 'Install the' with a blinking cursor; it is big, mostly empty black and repeated three times. The promised 'the hook stops the read' moment never appeared in any screenshot, so it explains nothing.

findings.title: Docs menu and status line are the company's internal papers, not user help
findings.detail: Looking for what the hook matches, the Docs dropdown offers the brief, memo, corrections, reality and team pages, and Start here carries a grey status paragraph with 'shipped v0.2.1' tags and 'SG Meter from api.newsroom.sgit.ai'. For a developer in a hurry this is noise sitting where he expects the answer.
